label: Abstract-only population of the selected world
definition: OnlyNonConcreteExistAt m concrete w holds when some candidate exists at w and no candidate existing at w is concrete: (∃ b, m.ExistsAt w b) ∧ ∀ b, m.ExistsAt w b → ¬ concrete b. Ordinary meaning: the world has an inventory, and all of it is non-concrete. Example: a world whose inventory is numbers and structures only. It is not the empty world, and it does not say concrete things are impossible.
note: Analyst framework definition of a rival position; attribution deferred. Motivated by abstract-only ontologies (Pythagorean or mathematical-structure monism). Rival of the population premise InhabitedConcreteAt on the same Ontic model, concrete predicate and world. Stronger than the negation of that premise: it adds that something exists at w. 'Concrete' is the supplied predicate; under the adopted sense it means having esse in re, so the rival says the existents of w lack esse in re. Whether Ontic existence may outrun esse in re is the open question this rival presses.
